summary.text: Alicia Malay is a Republican state representative from Vermont's Rutland-8 District who has served since January 2025 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. She is self-employed and lists lowering property taxes, public safety and economic growth as her priorities.

paragraphs.text: Alicia Malay graduated from Orville H. Platt High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Castleton College in 2014.
Her career experience includes being self-employed.
Malay assumed office on January 8, 2025, and advanced from the Republican primary on August 11, 2026.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a mother of three sons who has long been active in her community and as a moderate Republican seeking re-election to continue work on lowering property taxes, increasing public safety and growing the economy.

She said education makes up the majority of a property owner's tax bill and that education spending has risen sharply while enrollment has declined, and she said sentencing and treatment options are needed to address what she called a revolving door for many offenders.
She also said regulatory reform should make Vermont more business friendly, and she named criminal justice, corrections and public safety as her area of greatest policy interest.
